pull_requests.title: feat(openfeature): support opt-out from future experiments
pull_requests.body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds `ExperimentationOptOutFutureExperimentsOnly` and the environment value `future_experiments_only`.

For a subject with `dd_experimentation_opt_out_at`, compare the cutoff with each exposure-logging allocation's `randomizationActivatedAt`:

| Allocation activation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Before the cutoff | Continue normal evaluation and exposure logging. |
| At or after the cutoff, or unknown | Skip the allocation and continue ordinary delivery. |

Ordinary allocations remain eligible. Missing subject input preserves normal evaluation. Malformed subject input returns `INVALID_CONTEXT`, as in immediate mode. No new telemetry or subject history is added.

```sh
DD_FEATURE_FLAGS_EXPERIMENTATION_OPT_OUT_MODE=future_experiments_only
```

```go
// ProviderConfig{} uses the environment setting.
provider, err := ddflags.NewDatadogProvider(ddflags.ProviderConfig{})
if err != nil {
    return err
}
if err := of.SetNamedProviderAndWait("flags", provider); err != nil {
    return err
}
client := of.NewClient("flags")
attributes := map[string]any{}
if subject.ExperimentationOptOutAt != nil {
    attributes["dd_experimentation_opt_out_at"] =
        subject.ExperimentationOptOutAt.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339Nano)
}
enabled, err := client.BooleanValue(ctx, "new-route-planner", false,
    of.NewEvaluationContext(subject.ID, attributes))
```

An explicit `ProviderConfig{ExperimentationOptOutMode: ddflags.ExperimentationOptOutFutureExperimentsOnly}` overrides the environment setting.

### Motivation

Customers can stop new experiment participation while continuing older experiments. The cutoff describes allocation activation, not previous subject enrollment. An older experiment can still assign a subject for the first time.

**Stack:** #5666 supplies immediate mode and the configuration API. This PR adds the activation comparison. [Shared fixtures #52](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/pull/52) defines 42 capability checks; update the pin after that PR merges.

Enablement depends on the backend emitting stable activation metadata and retaining ordinary fallbacks. This PR does not deploy those changes. Allocations without metadata are skipped for opted-out subjects.

### Test coverage

Shared fixtures cover cutoff boundaries, timezone offsets, fractional seconds, invalid input, missing metadata, and fallback delivery. Local tests cover malformed activation metadata and valid-neighbor isolation in all modes, refresh, exposure deduplication, telemetry independence, and concurrent randomized subjects. Baseline and immediate-mode behavior remain covered. A benchmark covers all three modes.

[System tests #8135](https://github.com/DataDog/system-tests/pull/8135), stacked on system-tests #8080, add Remote Config, holdout assignment, exposure, and telemetry checks across all three modes. Release gating remains provisional until supported SDK releases are known.

### Validation

| Tested commit | Validation | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dd-trace-go@febcc185d27d8edbe4acf16ce2dee91d5aff730c` | System tests: disabled, immediate, and future-only modes; cutoff boundaries, Remote Config refresh, holdout assignments, exposure deduplication, and independent evaluation telemetry. Linux/amd64; `system-tests@6418472371431d01fbdb26cd220b90cd04077aa9`. | 12 passed; 0 failed; 0 skipped. |

### Reviewer's Checklist

- [ ] Changed code has unit tests for its functionality at or near 100% coverage.
- [ ] [System-Tests](https://github.com/DataDog/system-tests/) covering this feature have been added and enabled with the va.b.c-dev version tag.
- [ ] There is a benchmark for any new code, or changes to existing code.
- [ ] If this interacts with the agent in a new way, a system test has been added.
- [ ] New code is free of linting errors. You can check this by running `make lint` locally.
- [ ] New code doesn't break existing tests. You can check this by running `make test` locally.
- [ ] Add an appropriate team label so this PR gets put in the right place for the release notes.
- [ ] All generated files are up to date. You can check this by running `make generate` locally.
- [ ] Non-trivial go.mod changes, e.g. adding new modules, are reviewed by @DataDog/dd-trace-go-guild. Make sure all nested modules are up to date by running `make fix-modules` locally.

inline_comments.body: Fixed in febcc185d27d8edbe4acf16ce2dee91d5aff730c. The mode check now returns before reading allocation fields when exclusion is inactive, including when the subject attribute is absent. Ten alternating local benchmark samples show the disabled exclusion check improving from 2.304 ns to 2.044 ns. Whole-evaluation benchmarks showed no significant difference locally; the next CI benchmark must confirm whether its reported regression is removed.

inline_comments.body: Documented in febcc185d27d8edbe4acf16ce2dee91d5aff730c. Malformed activation metadata rejects only the affected flag, which returns the application default with PARSE_ERROR. Other valid flags remain usable. Expanded the parsing test to cover all three modes and verify valid-neighbor evaluation. This preserves the existing per-flag parsing behavior; it does not introduce configuration-wide rejection.

🤖 **Comment from Claude working with Aaron:** **[P0]** Please guard this call at the call site. Moving the mode check inside `excludes` did not remove the regression. With go1.27.3, `excludes` still does not inline: `cannot inline experimentationExclusion.excludes: function too complex: cost 106 exceeds budget 80`. So every allocation this loop visits pays a call, even in `disabled` mode, which is the default. The CI benchmark comment for `febcc185` still reports the same 7 regressions, from +2.1% to +6.7%.
Evidence — CI on febcc185 against de399851, and the earlier local run - `BenchmarkConcurrentEvaluations` +3.5% to +5.3% - `BenchmarkEvaluationWithVaryingContextSize` 1, 5, 10 and 20 fields: +2.2% to +6.7% - `BenchmarkEvaluationWithVaryingFlagCounts/5flags` +2.7% to +5.0% - `BenchmarkIntEvaluation` +2.1% to +3.0% An earlier interleaved run in this review, on `fdfd0913` (12 rounds, `-cpu 1`), measured +4.17% geomean against #5666 and +0.20% with this guard. The CI regressions at `febcc185` match that run. Later local re-runs were too noisy to resolve, so the next CI run should confirm the guard.
Suggested fix — the zero exclusion skips the call ```diff --- a/openfeature/evaluator.go +++ b/openfeature/evaluator.go @@ -73,7 +73,8 @@ func evaluateFlag(flag *flag, defaultValue any, context map[string]any, now time for _, allocation := range flag.Allocations { // Match the existing exposure-logging default when doLog is omitted. // Exclude before targeting or sharding, without changing eligible subjects' buckets. - if exclusion.excludes(allocation) { + // The zero exclusion (opt-out disabled or no timestamp) skips the call; excludes does not inline. + if exclusion.mode != ExperimentationOptOutDefault && exclusion.excludes(allocation) { continue } split, matched, err := evaluateAllocation(allocation, context, now) ``` `excludes` can keep its own mode check. The full package and `-race` pass.

inline_comments.body:
🤖 **Comment from Claude working with Aaron:** **[P2]** Please clarify the future-cutoff sentence so that customers send the opt-out time, not a later date. "A future cutoff does not schedule exclusion" can read as "nothing changes until that date". In fact a cutoff of 2027-10-19 keeps every allocation activated before it eligible, including experiments launched after the subject opted out. Targeting and schedules still apply. A customer who sends a later "effective date" leaves the subject eligible for those experiments.
Evidence — excludes() at this head ```text cutoff=2027-10-19 activation=2026-10-01T00:00:00Z excludes=false cutoff=2027-10-19 activation=2027-11-01T00:00:00Z excludes=true ``` The shared fixtures README uses similar wording ("A future cutoff is used directly; it does not schedule a future preference change"), so it may need the same clarification.
Suggested text ```diff --- a/openfeature/doc.go +++ b/openfeature/doc.go @@ -174,8 +174,10 @@ // // The cutoff is not an enrollment record: an older experiment can still assign a // subject for the first time. Configuration edits do not freeze targeting or values. -// Holdouts use the same activation cutoff. A future cutoff does not schedule exclusion; -// it permits allocations activated before that cutoff. Remove the attribute to opt back in. +// Holdouts use the same activation cutoff. A cutoff later than the evaluation time +// keeps every allocation activated before it eligible, including experiments launched +// after the subject opted out. Supply the time the subject opted out, not a later date. +// Remove the attribute to opt back in. // // This mode requires activation metadata from the configuration producer. Legacy // allocations without it are skipped for opted-out subjects, not treated as older. ```

+func TestExperimentationOptOutFutureExposures(t *testing.T) {
+	cutoff, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339Nano, experimentOptOutTestTime)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	for _, tc := range []struct {
+		name       string
+		activation *time.Time
+		doLog      *bool
+		continues  bool
+		exposures  int
+	}{
+		{"older experiment", new(cutoff.Add(-time.Second)), new(true), true, 2},
+		{"older experiment with default doLog", new(cutoff.Add(-time.Second)), nil, true, 2},
+		{"equal activation", new(cutoff), new(true), false, 1},
+		{"newer activation", new(cutoff.Add(time.Second)), new(true), false, 1},
+		{"unknown activation", nil, new(true), false, 1},
+		{"ordinary allocation", nil, new(false), true, 0},
+	} {
+		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			h := newOptOutHarness(t, ProviderConfig{
+				ExperimentationOptOutMode:                ExperimentationOptOutFutureExperimentsOnly,
+				EnableEvaluationTelemetryOptOutParameter: new(true),
+			})
+			a := h.provider.configuration.Flags["experiment"].Allocations[0]
+			a.RandomizationActivatedAt, a.DoLog = tc.activation, tc.doLog
+			h.evaluate(t, "enrolled", nil)
+			attrs := map[string]any{experimentationOptOutAtAttribute: experimentOptOutTestTime}
+			for _, subject := range []string{"enrolled", "enrolled", "first-evaluation"} {
+				details, err := h.client.BooleanValueDetails(context.Background(), "experiment", false,
+					of.NewEvaluationContext(subject, attrs))
+				require.NoError(t, err)
+				assert.Equal(t, tc.continues, details.Value)
+			}
+			// Restoring consent does not invalidate an unchanged exposure cache entry.
+			h.evaluate(t, "enrolled", nil)
+			h.provider.exposureWriter.flush()
+			assert.Len(t, h.sink.exposures, tc.exposures, "normal deduplication; no withdrawal event")
+			for _, exposure := range h.sink.exposures {
+				assert.Equal(t, "allocation", exposure.Allocation.Key)
+				assert.Equal(t, "on", exposure.Variant.Key)
+			}
+			h.provider.flagEvalLoggingWriter.drainAndFlush()
+			var count int64
+			for _, event := range h.sink.events {
+				count += event.EvaluationCount
+			}
+			assert.Equal(t, int64(5), count, "experimentation opt-out does not suppress evaluations")
+		})
+	}
+}
+
+func TestExperimentationOptOutFutureTelemetryIndependence(t *testing.T) {
+	h := newOptOutHarness(t, ProviderConfig{
+		ExperimentationOptOutMode:                ExperimentationOptOutFutureExperimentsOnly,
+		EnableEvaluationTelemetryOptOutParameter: new(true),
+	})
+	old := time.Date(2026, 10, 1, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	h.provider.configuration.Flags["experiment"].Allocations[0].RandomizationActivatedAt = &old
+	h.evaluate(t, "subject", map[string]any{
+		experimentationOptOutAtAttribute: experimentOptOutTestTime,
+		optOutTestParameter:              true,
+	})
+	h.assertCounts(t, 0, 1, 1)
+}
+
+func TestExperimentationOptOutFutureConfigurationRefresh(t *testing.T) {
+	h := newOptOutHarness(t, ProviderConfig{ExperimentationOptOutMode: ExperimentationOptOutFutureExperimentsOnly})
+	old := time.Date(2026, 10, 1, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	h.provider.configuration.Flags["experiment"].Allocations[0].RandomizationActivatedAt = &old
+	attrs := map[string]any{experimentationOptOutAtAttribute: experimentOptOutTestTime}
+	h.evaluate(t, "subject", attrs)
+
+	// A later configuration date and an edited schedule do not create a new run.
+	data, err := json.Marshal(h.provider.configuration)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	var refreshed universalFlagsConfiguration
+	require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal(data, &refreshed))
+	refreshed.CreatedAt = old.AddDate(1, 0, 0)
+	refreshed.Flags["experiment"].Allocations[0].StartAt = new(old.AddDate(-1, 0, 0))
+	h.provider.mu.Lock()
+	h.provider.configuration = &refreshed
+	h.provider.mu.Unlock()
+	h.evaluate(t, "subject", attrs)
+	h.evaluate(t, "new-subject", attrs)
+
+	// A new allocation has its own activation timestamp.
+	refreshed.Flags["experiment"].Allocations[0].Key = "new-allocation"
+	refreshed.Flags["experiment"].Allocations[0].RandomizationActivatedAt = new(old.AddDate(0, 1, 0))
+	result, err := h.client.BooleanValueDetails(context.Background(), "experiment", false, of.NewEvaluationContext("subject", attrs))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	assert.False(t, result.Value)
+	assert.Equal(t, of.DefaultReason, result.Reason)
+	h.provider.exposureWriter.flush()
+	assert.Len(t, h.sink.exposures, 2, "refresh did not create a new exposure for the existing subject")
+}
+
+func TestExperimentationOptOutFutureInput(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, tc := range []struct {
+		name  string
+		value any
+	}{
+		{"malformed", "invalid"},
+		{"empty", ""},
+		{"null", nil},
+		{"boolean", false},
+		{"number", 123},
+		{"array", []any{experimentOptOutTestTime}},
+		{"object", map[string]any{"timestamp": experimentOptOutTestTime}},
+	} {
+		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			exclusion, err := ExperimentationOptOutFutureExperimentsOnly.exclusion(map[string]any{experimentationOptOutAtAttribute: tc.value})
+			require.ErrorIs(t, err, errInvalidContext)
+			assert.Equal(t, experimentationExclusion{}, exclusion)
+		})
+	}
+}
+
+func TestExperimentationOptOutFutureActivationParsing(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, tc := range []struct {
+		name    string
+		raw     string
+		valid   bool
+		unknown bool
+	}{
+		{"missing", "", true, true},
+		{"null", ",\"randomizationActivatedAt\":null", true, true},
+		{"timestamp", ",\"randomizationActivatedAt\":\"2026-10-01T12:00:00Z\"", true, false},
+		{"malformed", ",\"randomizationActivatedAt\":\"invalid\"", false, false},
+		{"empty", ",\"randomizationActivatedAt\":\"\"", false, false},
+		{"number", ",\"randomizationActivatedAt\":123", false, false},
+		{"boolean", ",\"randomizationActivatedAt\":true", false, false},
+		{"array", ",\"randomizationActivatedAt\":[]", false, false},
+		{"object", ",\"randomizationActivatedAt\":{}", false, false},
+	} {
+		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			var config universalFlagsConfiguration
+			require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal([]byte(`{"format":"SERVER","flags":{
+				"test":{"key":"test","enabled":true,"variationType":"BOOLEAN",
+				"variations":{"on":{"key":"on","value":true}},
+				"allocations":[{"key":"a","doLog":true,"splits":[{"variationKey":"on","shards":[]}]`+tc.raw+`}]},
+				"neighbor":{"key":"neighbor","enabled":true,"variationType":"BOOLEAN",
+				"variations":{"on":{"key":"on","value":true}},
+				"allocations":[{"key":"a","doLog":false,"splits":[{"variationKey":"on","shards":[]}]}]}
+			}}`), &config))
+			assert.Contains(t, config.Flags, "neighbor")
+			if tc.valid {
+				require.Contains(t, config.Flags, "test")
+				assert.Equal(t, tc.unknown, config.Flags["test"].Allocations[0].RandomizationActivatedAt == nil)
+			} else {
+				require.NotContains(t, config.Flags, "test")
+				for _, mode := range []ExperimentationOptOutMode{
+					ExperimentationOptOutDisabled,
+					ExperimentationOptOutImmediate,
+					ExperimentationOptOutFutureExperimentsOnly,
+				} {
+					exclusion, err := mode.exclusion(map[string]any{experimentationOptOutAtAttribute: experimentOptOutTestTime})
+					require.NoError(t, err)
+					result := evaluateConfiguredFlag(&config, "test", false, nil, time.Now(), exclusion)
+					assert.ErrorIs(t, result.Error, errParseError)
+					assert.Equal(t, false, result.Value)
+					neighbor := evaluateConfiguredFlag(&config, "neighbor", false, nil, time.Now(), exclusion)
+					assert.NoError(t, neighbor.Error)
+					assert.Equal(t, true, neighbor.Value)
+				}
+			}
+		})
+	}
+}
+
+func TestExperimentationOptOutFutureConcurrentBuckets(t *testing.T) {
+	h := newOptOutHarness(t, ProviderConfig{ExperimentationOptOutMode: ExperimentationOptOutFutureExperimentsOnly})
+	f := h.provider.configuration.Flags["experiment"]
+	activation := time.Date(2026, 10, 19, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
+	f.Allocations[0].RandomizationActivatedAt = &activation
+	f.Variations["off"] = &variant{Key: "off", Value: false}
+	f.Allocations[0].Splits = []*split{
+		{VariationKey: "on", Shards: []*shard{{Salt: "holdout", TotalShards: 10000, Ranges: []*shardRange{{Start: 0, End: 1000}}}}},
+		{VariationKey: "off", Shards: []*shard{{Salt: "holdout", TotalShards: 10000, Ranges: []*shardRange{{Start: 1000, End: 10000}}}}},
+	}
+	var wg sync.WaitGroup
+	var groups sync.Map
+	for i := range 100 {
+		wg.Go(func() {
+			attrs := of.FlattenedContext{of.TargetingKey: strconv.Itoa(i)}
+			baseline := h.provider.BooleanEvaluation(context.Background(), "experiment", false, attrs)
+			assert.NotEmpty(t, baseline.Variant)
+			groups.Store(baseline.Variant, true)
+			attrs[experimentationOptOutAtAttribute] = activation.Add(time.Second).Format(time.RFC3339Nano)
+			continued := h.provider.BooleanEvaluation(context.Background(), "experiment", false, attrs)
+			assert.Equal(t, baseline.Value, continued.Value)
+			assert.Equal(t, baseline.Variant, continued.Variant)
+			assert.Equal(t, baseline.Reason, continued.Reason)
+			attrs[experimentationOptOutAtAttribute] = activation.Format(time.RFC3339Nano)
+			excluded := h.provider.BooleanEvaluation(context.Background(), "experiment", false, attrs)
+			assert.Equal(t, of.DefaultReason, excluded.Reason)
+			assert.Empty(t, excluded.Variant)
+		})
+	}
+	wg.Wait()
+	_, on := groups.Load("on")
+	_, off := groups.Load("off")
+	assert.True(t, on && off, "both randomized groups must be exercised")
+}

🤖 **Comment from Codex working with Leo:** **Decision: align Go with the browser's scoped activation-error policy.** Thanks, Aaron — agreed that malformed activation metadata should not break evaluations for customers who have not enabled future-mode opt-out. We settled this in [the browser decision thread](https://github.com/DataDog/openfeature-js-client/pull/423#discussion_r4348001493), implemented at `3704387`. You then [confirmed the Node probe and four scope tests](https://github.com/DataDog/openfeature-js-client/pull/423#discussion_r4348262068). **Implemented in [c5fec6a009ffa29bf53f5377a21856c7c4aa5f56](https://github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/commit/c5fec6a009ffa29bf53f5377a21856c7c4aa5f56).** Go now parses activation once when configuration arrives, preserves **valid / missing / invalid** states, and consumes the invalid state only for an opted-out subject in `future_experiments_only`.
Behavior — the distinction we are preserving | Situation | Result | | --- | --- | | Opt-out disabled, immediate mode, or no subject cutoff | Bad activation does not introduce an error; retain that mode's normal behavior. | | Future mode + valid subject cutoff + malformed activation | Application default with `PARSE_ERROR` for the affected flag; other valid flags remain usable. | | Future mode + valid subject cutoff + missing/null activation | Skip that exposure-logging allocation and continue to the next allocation. | The deliberate tradeoff is keeping malformed metadata visible when this policy depends on it. For an opted-out future-mode subject, the flag errors even if the malformed allocation is unreachable or an ordinary fallback exists. Your invalid-as-missing proposal would allow that fallback; we're retaining the browser distinction here.
Native validation — local checks at c5fec6a009ff - Full `go test ./openfeature/ -count=1` and `go test -race ./openfeature/ -count=1` pass, including the PR-pinned shared fixtures. - All **90 applicable Lean policy cases** pass through the actual Go configuration decoder and provider. The adapter checks both error codes and selected variants, so returning the default cannot impersonate ordinary fallback delivery. - Regression coverage includes all modes, absent cutoffs, malformed types, unreachable and non-logging allocations, valid neighboring flags, strict `startAt`/`endAt` decoding, and invalid → valid → null → invalid updates through Remote Config and the OpenFeature client. - The new tests fail against the previous all-mode rejection and an invalid-as-missing mutation. An independent review found no remaining issues in the scoped diff and adapter. These are local native checks. Timestamp grammar, the other contract families, CI and system-tests at this new commit remain separate evidence; this update does not claim the other review threads are addressed.
Sneak preview — turning review decisions into reusable, checked SDK contracts We're building a small “proof” workflow around exactly this kind of cross-SDK review: 1. **A versioned English decision** (`D004`, revision 2), linked to where it was set. 2. **An executable Lean model**, with checked statements about the rule. 3. **Shared oracle cases** that native SDK adapters can run against pinned source revisions. 4. **A linked history of evidence**, preserving passing and failing checks separately from the decision's authority. For example, this theorem is already checked in the local model: ```lean theorem only_future_cutoff_needs_activation (m : Mode) (a : Attribute) (t : Activation) (logging : Bool) : (policy m a t logging).error = .parseError ↔ m = .future ∧ a = .valid ∧ t = .invalid := by cases m <;> cases a <;> cases t <;> simp [policy, normal] ``` In plain English: within this activation-policy model, `PARSE_ERROR` occurs exactly when future mode, a valid subject cutoff, and invalid activation coincide. Other configuration errors are outside this theorem. The local prototype currently passes **36 theorem audits and 313 oracle cases** across the broader opt-out contract. It also checks a concrete counterexample showing that invalid-as-missing and the browser policy differ. The useful result is a reviewable rule that we can carry between PRs, with an evidence trail showing which SDK revision was tested against it. The Lean proof establishes properties of the model. This Go change now has separate native conformance and regression evidence, tied to the commit above; the prototype and broader fleet adoption remain separate.
